correctness.rationale: The p-torsion subgroup is C_p^2, giving p+1 order-p lines; element counting gives exactly p cyclic order-p^2 subgroups, all with common order-p subgroup P, plus the unique elementary abelian order-p^2 subgroup. Their intersections give exactly a clique K_{p+2} with p pendant leaves at its p-torsion center. A zero forcing complement cannot contain two leaves or two noncentral clique vertices, and with at most one of each class a blue leaf can first force a white center, then a blue clique vertex clears the possible white clique vertex and the center clears the possible white leaf. The complement enumerator is therefore (1+pt)(1+(p+1)t)(1+t), yielding the stated polynomial. The packaged verifier exhaustively checks the criterion for p=2,3,5,7 and directly enumerates actual subgroups for p=2,3.

originality.rationale: Known pineapple results already imply minimum rank 3 and the scalar zero forcing number m+k-3; these are not treated as new. The checked subgroup-intersection and zero-forcing-polynomial literature did not provide the all-zero-forcing-set classification or complete pineapple polynomial. The accepted claim adds the factored enumerator, exact minimizer classification, and its natural C_{p^2} times C_p subgroup-lattice realization.

value.rationale: C_{p^2} times C_p is the first finite abelian p-group family that is simultaneously noncyclic and non-elementary, so its subgroup intersection graph is a natural boundary object. The result gives the complete forcing-set enumerator and exact minimizers, not merely a scalar already known for abstract pineapples. The factorization directly reflects the three subgroup roles—pendant lines, noncentral clique subgroups, and the p-torsion center—and provides a compact benchmark for broader finite-abelian subgroup-intersection forcing problems.
